reason: E1 supports Al–Al clustering but does not mention Al–Ni clustering or negative mixing enthalpies; E2 supports high configurational entropy and sluggish diffusion suppressing precipitation, but neither source links clustering to improved mechanical properties or a clustering-to-ordering transition. Key premises about Al–Ni clustering, mobility reduction by clustering, and property outcomes are unsupported.
premises: Strongly negative mixing enthalpies (Al–Ni, Al–Al) drive local chemical clustering in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
High configurational entropy competes with positive mixing enthalpy to stabilize a single-phase solid solution.
Sluggish atomic diffusion in HEAs suppresses precipitation under irradiation.
Local clustering reduces atomic mobility and suppresses diffusion-driven phase separation.
Low-Al alloys exhibit persistent single-phase structure with Al-centered clusters and no brittle secondary phases.
